repositories.name: metadata-service
repositories.reason: Owns the metadata store: must add per-column classification (model, store, merge-on-reingest), suggest it from ingested column tags, expose a steward override endpoint, and include classification in GET columns and metadata.dataset.changed.v1.

repositories.name: platform-contracts
repositories.reason: Source of truth for event JSON Schemas and OpenAPI specs, so every changed contract (schema.discovered, dataset.changed, metadata-service, entitlements and query OpenAPI) is edited and released here first.

repositories.name: platform-sdk
repositories.reason: Shared typed clients (MetadataClient, entitlements client) and event helpers must expose the new classification fields, the override call and masked_columns in access decisions, then be released for consumers.

repositories.name: ingestion-service
repositories.reason: Discovers source schemas, and ingestion.schema.discovered.v1 currently carries only column name/type/nullable, so source column tags/comments must be added for classification suggestion (AC1).

repositories.name: entitlements-service
repositories.reason: Answers access decisions and must add a pii:read grant and return the PII columns to mask when the requester lacks it (AC3), using classifications from metadata.dataset.changed.v1 / metadata-service-api.

repositories.name: consumption-gateway
repositories.reason: Serves query results to data consumers and must mask the columns listed in the entitlements decision before returning results (AC4).

repositories.name: transformation-service
repositories.reason: Runs transformation rules and must read column classifications from metadata-service-api and apply PII-format validation rules to PII columns (AC5).

repositories.name: platform-e2e
repositories.reason: Cross-service end-to-end suite covering ingestion, metadata-service, entitlements, consumption-gateway and transformation-service needs new scenarios for the tag-to-classification-to-masking flow and the PII transformation rules.

repositories.name: search-indexer
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 and pins platform-contracts directly, so it must be re-verified against the additive column fields (strict schema validation could reject them).

repositories.name: lineage-service
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1, whose column objects gain new fields, so its deserialization must be re-verified.

repositories.name: notification-service
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata-service-api (additive response change) and transformation.result.published.v1, which will now include PII-rule failures, so it must be re-verified and checked that emails never include raw PII values.

considered_not_impacted.name: reporting-service
considered_not_impacted.reason: Listed as a dataset.changed consumer in the metadata-service README, but the catalog marks it decommissioned/archived with no events consumed; the README is stale and should be corrected in metadata-service.

considered_not_impacted.name: usage-metering
considered_not_impacted.reason: Only consumes consumption.access.logged.v1, which this plan leaves unchanged.

considered_not_impacted.name: platform-catalog
considered_not_impacted.reason: No new integration edges, topics or API entities are introduced (all changes extend existing contracts), so no catalog entity changes are needed; revisit if a new topic is chosen.

contracts.name: ingestion.schema.discovered.v1
contracts.description: Add optional columns[].tags (array of lower-case strings parsed from the source column comment, e.g. 'tags: pii,email' -> ["pii","email"]) and optional columns[].comment; schema in platform-contracts.

contracts.name: metadata.dataset.changed.v1
contracts.description: Add optional dataset.columns[].classification (PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII or null), classification_source (SUGGESTED|STEWARD) and tags; classification changes are emitted with the existing change_type COLUMNS_CHANGED, so the enum is not extended.

contracts.name: GET /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns
contracts.description: Each column object gains optional classification, classification_source, tags, classified_by and classified_at fields.

contracts.name: PUT /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns/{column}/classification
contracts.description: Steward sets or overrides one column's classification (body: {classification, reason}); stores it with source STEWARD, returns the column, and publishes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (COLUMNS_CHANGED); 400 on an unknown value, 404 on an unknown dataset or column, 403 without the steward grant.

contracts.name: POST /v1/access-decisions
contracts.description: Access decision response gains masked_columns (column names to mask; PII columns when the requester lacks pii:read) and an optional mask_policy; existing allow/deny fields unchanged. Path is inferred; the real path is in platform-contracts/openapi/entitlements-service.yaml.

contracts.name: POST /v1/queries
contracts.description: Result values of masked columns are replaced in a type-safe way (null or a fixed mask string for string columns), and the response gains optional masked_columns metadata; column set and order unchanged. Path is inferred; the real path is in platform-contracts/openapi/consumption-gateway.yaml.

open_questions: Does ingestion-service already capture source column comments/tags internally, and is the 'tags: a,b' comment convention the same across all connectors?

What is the exact tag-to-classification mapping and precedence (e.g. pii > confidential > internal > public), and does a suggestion apply to columns that have no tags (null vs a default such as INTERNAL)?
Should unclassified (null) columns be treated as not masked (fail-open, compatible) or masked (fail-closed) once enforcement is on?
Which grant authorizes stewards to call the classification override endpoint, and is it enforced in metadata-service or by the entitlements-service?
What are the exact entitlements-api and query-api paths and response shapes? They are not visible in this workspace; the paths used here are inferred.
Which mask representation do consumers accept (null, '***', partial masking, hashing), especially for non-string PII columns such as dates of birth?
Which PII-format rules (email, phone, national id, ...) should transformation-service apply, and does it need the PII subtype from tags (e.g. 'email') in addition to the PII classification?
Do any metadata.dataset.changed.v1 consumers or schema validators (search-indexer via platform-contracts) reject unknown properties (additionalProperties: false)?
Who must receive pii:read before masking is enforced so existing legitimate PII consumers are not broken, and who approves the list?
Should consumption.access.logged.v1 record which columns were masked for audit purposes? Not required by the ticket; if added it would affect usage-metering.
Should search-indexer index classification for catalog search/faceting? Not required by the acceptance criteria.
